content: 1. Administer a dose of 5 mg/kg orally every 12 hours for 7 days. Use only oral suspension or immediate-release tablets for children; do not use extended-release formulations. 2. The combination of alfuzosin and clarithromycin increases the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 3. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 4. Clarithromycin and cisapride both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Clarithromycin and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Co-administration of conivaptan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 8. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Co-administration may result in vasospasm and ischemia of extremities and other tissues, including the central nervous system. 9. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of intranasal dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Co-administration may result in vasospasm and ischemia of extremities and other tissues, including the central nervous system. 10. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. Reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily in extensive metabolizers. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are given concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 14. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Co-administration may result in vasospasm and ischemia of extremities and other tissues, including the central nervous system. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. Severe hypotension or syncope can occur. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 18. Clarithromycin and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 19. Clarithromycin and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Co-administration of ivabradine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Lomitapide levels may increase several folds. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase systemic statin exposure and the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Increased lurasidone exposure may lead to serious adverse reactions. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase mavacamten systemic exposure, resulting in heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can significantly increase naloxegol systemic exposure, potentially precipitating opioid withdrawal symptoms. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 29. Clarithromycin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 30. Clarithromycin and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases pimozide levels by decreasing its metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 31. Quinidine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. This is contraindicated. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels of rifabutin by decreasing its metabolism. This is contraindicated. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. There is an increased risk of rhabdomyolysis with drugs that increase simvastatin systemic exposure. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. Use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated with venetoclax during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75%. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt treatment with acalabrutinib. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib concentrations have reached steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not reached, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors will increase adagrasib concentrations and its toxicities. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. DM1, the cytotoxic component, is metabolized mainly by CYP3A4; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. This combination may result in QT interval prolongation. 43. Amiodarone and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin and amisulpride both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Amitriptyline and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Amoxapine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Clarithromycin and anagrelide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Clarithromycin increases the effects of antithrombin alfa by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin increases the effects of antithrombin III by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if co-administration is necessary. Adjust the dose according to prescribing information if needed. 51. Apomorphine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Clarithromycin increases the effects of argatroban by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Aripiprazole and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Arsenic trioxide and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Artemether and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Clarithromycin and asenapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Asenapine transdermal and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Atomoxetine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 61. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Do not exceed an atorvastatin dose of 20 mg/day when co-administered with clarithromycin. 62. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure to avanafil, which may result in significant adverse events, including severe hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 63. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of avapritinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 64. Clarithromycin increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unable to avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 65. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete to administer live bacterial vaccines. 67. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of bedaquiline with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit of treatment outweighs the risk. 68. Clarithromycin increases the effects of bemiparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 69. Clarithromycin increases the effects of bivalirudin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 70. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor cannot be avoided, reduce the brigatinib once-daily dose by about 50% (e.g., from 180 mg to 90 mg, or from 90 mg to 60 mg). After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor, resume the brigatinib dose that was tolerated prior to initiating the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 73. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 74. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 75. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
